isolatedNativeBoundaries.cohortDefinition: All 300 unclaimed singleton boundary requests from the six first-region native inputs, each routed alone with all original obstacles/rules; 10 seconds per request. These are isolated requests, not jointly complete boards.

fanout31.interpretation: The change affects none of the 72 frozen routing preparations. These workers hit different 120-second deadlines, including losses and gains, even between identical baseline versions. Their 9 → 10 counts do not establish a routing gain. All completed SVGs match the canonical baseline; raw reports retain every timeout.

selectedFix.problem: Displacement from a source pad can select a direction different from the single boundary edge already touched by the target copper.
selectedFix.change: Use that unique common boundary edge as the default direction for ordinary boundary requests; preserve explicit directions, preferred exits, available regions and plane policy. Corners/interior/outside targets keep displacement inference.
selectedFix.existingEndpointPolicy: These are automatic breakout points: core already relocates them to each emitted boundary exit. The change does not force the original target coordinate.
selectedFix.decision: Choose the +12 net isolated accepts (+5.1%) and 15 fewer distinct drills over the CPU-only alternative. This is a net heuristic improvement, with one real OrangeCrab loss and no complete-board gain; no speedup claimed.

knownRegression.before: down direction, solved with one via
knownRegression.cause: Both existing rightward dogbone via sites intersect C4 bottom pads. The old down direction accesses the legal opposite interstice. The new default is a heuristic and does not improve every request.

alternativeCandidate.change: Memoize immutable plane source paths and static string prefixes within each route call while retaining ordered clearance-cache lookups.
alternativeCandidate.decision: Deferred. It improves native medians by 26.8–29.8% with unchanged routes, but adds no accepted native request. The selected default-direction change improves routing yield and reduces aggregate drills.

limits: All six full boards still fail their first fanout region. Fanout precedes bus lanes and the remaining router; no DDR bus phase starts.
Best partial escape counts are uncommitted search states, not connected full-board nets or committed PCB copper.
OrangeCrab reaches 27 → 19 assignments at the 600-second cutoff and H616 after reaches 227/256; these partial counts are not matched timing measurements.

Boundary totals route one request at a time with complete original obstacles. Shared routing competition can change gains and via counts: joint U22 uses 7 → 8 vias while its best partial improves 7 → 9 escapes.
Three serial matched pairs per native scene alternate before/after order on one Blacksmith worker. Selected-candidate native medians rise about 3.1% / 0.1%, so no runtime improvement is claimed.
Original copper is removed; native source geometry and design rules are retained.
